subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in fail-closed `cron.minInterval` config that rejects and paces recurring schedules below an operator-selected floor?
rationale: The code path is coherent, but root policy treats new config/default surfaces and fail-closed scheduling behavior as compatibility-sensitive product decisions rather than routine implementation details.

options.title: Approve the opt-in guardrail
options.body: Keep the enforceable config surface because unset config preserves default behavior, then require docs-map regeneration and exact-head green proof before merge.

options.title: Switch to warning-only guidance
options.body: Prefer the lower-risk warning-only direction if maintainers do not want cron creation/update to reject schedules under an operator floor.

options.title: Defer cadence policy
options.body: Pause or close this PR until cron operator controls are revisited as a broader scheduling policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in guardrail
recommendation.body: Keep the enforceable config surface because unset config preserves default behavior, then require docs-map regeneration and exact-head green proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` is both assigned and the strongest recent owner signal for the central cron service paths affected by the policy choice.
